With Cache

with_cache.Rd

Runs an expression with cache.

Usage

with_cache(
  expr,
  path = Sys.getenv("R_IKER_CACHE_PATH"),
  timeout = 8,
  force = FALSE,
  limit = 1,
  cleanup = c("auto", "off"),
  encrypt = TRUE,
  key = Sys.getenv("R_IKER_CACHE_KEY"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

expr

an expression to evaluate.

path

the path to the cache folder.

timeout

a numeric (in hours) to indicate when cache content is expired.

force

a logical, if cache content should be updated.

limit

a numeric, the cache size limit (in Mb).

cleanup

a character string or a numeric value (see details).

encrypt

a logical, if cache content should be encrypted.

key

a character string, to be used as a secret.

verbose

a logical, if logs should be printed.

Value

whatever the evaluation of expr produces.

Details

Even though the function is designed to work with call_api(), it could in principle work with any expression.

When a single location is used to store the cache content, the "R_IKER_CACHE_PATH" is recommended to define path.

When force = TRUE, the expression will be run even if the cache content is not expired.

By default cleanup is set to "auto". The function will check whether the files in cache are older than the timeout. Obsolete files will be deleted. This behavior can be turned off with cleanup = "off" or tuned with a numeric value cleanup = 24 in hours.

By default, encrypt is set to TRUE so that cache content is encrypted. This is because many APIs require a key/token as an authentication method to access their resources.

Setting encrypt = FALSE exposes the content of the cache files. It should only be used for APIs that do not require an authentication (an open source geocoding service for example).

When encrypt = TRUE, a key is mandatory to encode/decode the content of the cache. The expected value is a character string that does NOT need to be hashed. This value will be used to generate the actual encryption key. That being said, this key should not be hard coded or an easy one to find. The rstring() function can be used to generate one, but the generated value needs to be saved and passed to the "R_IKER_CACHE_KEY" environment variable. If the key is lost, the cache content is lost.

See also

rstring()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# set R_IKER_CACHE_PATH environment variable
# set R_IKER_CACHE_KEY environment variable

# basic example:
# first call will evaluate & return the current time
with_cache(Sys.time(), verbose = T)
# next calls will return cache content (for 8 hours)
with_cache(Sys.time(), verbose = T)
} # }
